title: clear-docker-cache should not breack running jobs
description:
## Description

Actually [clear-docker-cache](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/blob/main/packaging/root/usr/share/gitlab-runner/clear-docker-cache) can break job as it can remove network or containeres in between 

This can cause problems when running the script at the same time that a job is running on the runner.

```
Uploading artifacts for successful job
00:01
Using effective pull policy of [always] for container sha256:4e31107846926fc4c8a4be4b742dd9ddecb2973408f5e38a38c7f970e409cdd0
ERROR: Container "1e4fe212d115ca60dda7be3cab4d210e53475c50ec814818f8eeab579053ff45" not found or removed. Will retry...
Cleaning up project directory and file based variables
00:00
ERROR: Container "1e4fe212d115ca60dda7be3cab4d210e53475c50ec814818f8eeab579053ff45" not found or removed. Will retry...
ERROR: network inspect returned error  Error response from daemon: network f604e99769da9c07005b523652d3c31a103ea55a7733b8fb726bdf25d87d33e5 not found (manager.go:112:0s)
ERROR: Job failed (system failure): Error response from daemon: network runner-zozdhy4pv-3704-3-5076585 not found (exec.go:75:0s)
```

## Proposal

It would make sense to have a way to check if a job is currently running and not run the script in that case. With FF_NETWORK_PER_BUILD this could be done by checking if the network exist or not.

description:

- **Action** — MR links, or why no action is needed

> ⚠️ **Removal caveat.** Not every flag is read through the `featureflags` package. `FF_USE_DIRECT_DOWNLOAD` is consumed via a struct tag (`env:"FF_USE_DIRECT_DOWNLOAD"` at [`commands/helpers/artifacts_downloader.go:28`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/blob/main/commands/helpers/artifacts_downloader.go#L28)), so the `featureflags.UseDirectDownload` constant has **no production references at all**. A removal MR that greps for the Go identifier will conclude the flag is dead code and silently break direct download. Every removal must grep for the literal `FF_` string.

GitLab descriptions are last-write-wins with no merge, so two people editing the table in the same window will silently clobber each other. Keep table edits to the single row you own, and treat your issue — not this description — as the authoritative record of your verdict.
